title: The 194-Year-Old Tortoise With Secrets in His DNA
summary:
Jonathan is a giant tortoise who is about 194 years old. Scientists believe he hatched in 1832, which means he was alive when Charles Darwin and Queen Victoria were alive. Today, he is the oldest known living land animal.

Scientists studied Jonathan's DNA, the tiny instructions inside his body that help decide how it works. They found 287 special changes in his DNA that may help protect him from aging. These changes help his body fix damaged DNA, calm swelling, control insulin, and fight cancer.

The scientists also looked at his epigenome, a set of chemical markers that switch genes on and off. These markers usually change as animals grow old, but in Jonathan, the ones that control DNA repair and energy stayed very steady.

Dr. Justin Gerlach of the University of Cambridge, who worked on the study, said these gene controllers have stayed incredibly stable for almost 200 years. The team hopes the findings may one day help scientists slow aging and prevent long-term diseases in people — but that will take much more research.
why_it_matters: Learning how Jonathan's body repairs itself could one day help doctors keep people healthier as they grow older.
